==概要== [[天岩戸]]開きの際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞い、後に[[ニニギノミコト]]が[[高千穂]]に降り立ったとき（[[天孫降臨]]）供をした[[アメノウズメ]]と[[地祇]]でニニギノミコトを先導した[[サルタヒコ]]の子孫。
名の由来はサルタヒコが醜男であり、猿の顔に似ていて、それと結婚したアメノウズメが猿女君と呼ばれたことからきている。
アメノウズメは[[巫女]]の始祖であり、猿女君氏も代々[[巫女]]や[[神職]]の仕事についてきた。
親戚に[[稗田]]氏がおり、[[古事記]]編纂にかかわった[[稗田阿礼]]も猿女君氏とは血縁関係にある。

余談ではあるが、漫画「朝霧の巫女」に登場する巫女三姉妹の姓も「稗田」であり、猿女君氏との関連性を示唆している。
==参考文献== 「古事記」[[太安万侶]]・編
「[[朝霧の巫女]]」[[宇川弘樹]]・著　[[少年画報社]]

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ）は、古代より[[朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきた[[氏族]]の一つである。[[アメノウズメ]]を始祖としている。
[[日本神話]]においてアメノウズメが[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った。氏族の名前は、アメノウズメが[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[サルタヒコ]]と応対したことにより、サルタヒコの名を残すために[[ニニギ]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く、[[弘仁]]年間には小野氏・和邇部氏が猿女君の養田を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあった。
[[古事記]]編纂にかかわった[[稗田阿礼]]を出した[[稗田氏]]は、猿女君とは血縁関係にある。
余談ではあるが、漫画「朝霧の巫女」（[[宇川弘樹]]・著 [[少年画報社]]）に登場する巫女三姉妹の姓も「稗田」であり、猿女君氏との関連性を示唆している。

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ・'''猨女君'''）は、古代より[[朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきた[[氏族]]の一つである。[[アメノウズメ]]を始祖としている<ref>『[[日本書紀]]』『[[古語拾遺]]』『[[先代旧事本紀]]』（天神本紀）</ref>。[[カバネ|姓]]は君。
[[日本神話]]においてアメノウズメが[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った猿女を貢進した氏族。氏族の名前は、アメノウズメが[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[サルタヒコ]]と応対したことにより、サルタヒコの名を残すために[[ニニギ]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している<ref>『古事記』</ref>。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定されるが、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]][[稗田村]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]]稗田町）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏|稗田]]姓を称した<ref>[[佐伯有清]]編『日本古代氏族事典』[[雄山閣出版]]、1994年、247頁</ref>。
他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇部氏]]が猿女君の養田を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあった<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。

他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあった<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ・'''猨女君'''、'''猿女公'''）は、古代より[[朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきたとされる一族。
== 概要 == [[アメノウズメ]]を始祖としており<ref>『[[古事記]]』『[[日本書紀]]』『[[古語拾遺]]』『[[先代旧事本紀]]』（[[天神本紀]]）</ref>{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}、[[君]]{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}を[[姓]]に持つ[[氏族]]の一つともされるが、君・公は女性への尊称であり、姓ではないともされる<ref>宝賀寿男「稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文」『古樹紀之房間』2015年</ref>。実際『[[姓氏録]]』等に猿女君を称する氏族は見られない。
[[日本神話]]においてアメノウズメが[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998|}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。氏族の名前は、アメノウズメが[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している<ref>『古事記』</ref>。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定されるが、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]][[稗田村]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
== 考証 == 他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる が<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>、一方で[[猿田毘古神]]は『古事記』に伝える[[宇都志日金折命]]、また穂高氏の祖神とされる穂高見命と同一視する説もあり<ref>神々の系譜と海神族の初期分岐過程</ref>、それに従えば所謂猿女君と和邇氏・小野氏は同族となり、横取りして猿女君を貢進したとは言えない。また猿女君は女性の尊称であるため、特定の氏族によって輩出されたとも限らない。

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ・'''猨女君'''、'''猿女公'''）は、古代より[[朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきたとされる一族。

本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定されるが、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]][[稗田村]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
== 考証 == 他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる が<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>、一方で[[猿田毘古神]]は『古事記』に伝える[[宇都志日金折命]]、また穂高氏の祖神とされる穂高見命と同一視する説もあり<ref>神々の系譜と海神族の初期分岐過程</ref>、それに従えば所謂猿女君と和邇氏・小野氏は同族となり、横取りして猿女君を貢進したとは言えない。また猿女君は女性の尊称であるため、特定の氏族によって輩出されたとも限らない。

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ・'''猨女君'''、'''猿女公'''）は、古代より[[朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきたとされる一族。
== 概要 == 天神[[天宇受売命]]を始祖としており<ref>『[[古事記]]』、『[[日本書紀]]』、『[[古語拾遺]]』、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』（天神本紀）</ref>{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}、[[君 (姓)|君]]{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}を[[姓]]に持つ[[氏族]]の一つともされるが、「君・公」は姓ではなく女性への尊称であり、また『[[新撰姓氏録]]』などに猿女君について何ら記録がないことから、実際には猿女君という氏族は存在せず、女官の称号であったとされる<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/kojikijo/jobunkou1.htm 稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文]」『古樹紀之房間』、2015年。</ref>。
[[日本神話]]において天宇受売命が[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998|}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。この名前は、天宇受売命が[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定されるが、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]][[稗田村]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
== 考証 == 他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされるが<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>、一方で[[猿田毘古神]]は『古事記』に伝える[[宇都志日金折命]]、また穂高氏の祖神とされる穂高見命と同一視する説もあり<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/shintoufu/shintoufu1.htm 神々の系譜と海神族の初期分岐過程]」『古樹紀之房間』、2011年。</ref>、それに従えば所謂猿女君と和邇氏・小野氏は同族となり、横取りして猿女君を貢進したとは言えない。また猿女君は女性の尊称であるため、特定の氏族によって輩出されたとも限らない。

== 概要 == [[天神]]・[[天宇受売命]]を始祖としており<ref>『[[古事記]]』、『[[日本書紀]]』、『[[古語拾遺]]』、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』（天神本紀）</ref>{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}、[[君 (カバネ)|君]]{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}を[[姓]]に持つ[[氏族]]の一つともされるが、「君・公」は姓ではなく女性への尊称であり、また『[[新撰姓氏録]]』などに猿女君について何ら記録がないこと、女性を始祖とする具体的な氏族の存在が確認できないことなどから、実際には猿女君という氏族は存在せず、女官の称号であったとする説もある<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/kojikijo/jobunkou1.htm 稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文]」『古樹紀之房間』、2015年。</ref>。
[[日本神話]]において天宇受売命が[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998|}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。この名前は、天宇受売命が[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定されるが、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]][[稗田村]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
== 考証 == {{要出典範囲|他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く|date=2021年5月}}、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。
一方、「蓋し神代記紀の猿女の話は神話に過ぎじ、小野氏が猿女を貢するは反って相当の理由ありしか」という意見もある{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。これを受けて、猿女の養田の所在地が[[近江国]]和邇村、[[山城国]]小野郷であることからも、和邇氏族の小野臣・和邇部臣両氏こそが主として猿女を輩出してきた氏族であると見る説もある。この説では、本来は[[猿田彦命]]・[[天宇受売命]]の後裔であった和邇氏族が、[[孝安天皇]]後裔の[[皇別]]氏族という系譜に変更されたことによって、猿女供出氏族ではないと主張したものとされる<ref>宝賀寿男「猿女君の意義 稗田阿禮の周辺（上）」『東アジアの古代文化』106号収録、[[大和書房]]、2001年、177-178頁。</ref>。

revision.comment: /* 概要 */『新撰姓氏録』に記されていない氏族なんて腐るほどいるのに、猿女君だけが「氏族ではないけど『君』付けで呼ばれる特殊な集団」である可能性ってどれくらいあるんでしょうか。 しかも『新撰姓氏録』には「山都多祁流比女命」の「四世孫毛能志乃和気命」の末裔を主張する阿刀部氏がいますし。

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ・'''猨女君'''、'''猿女公'''）は、古代より[[朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきたとされる一族。
== 概要 == [[天神]]・[[天宇受売命]]を始祖としており<ref>『[[古事記]]』、『[[日本書紀]]』、『[[古語拾遺]]』、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』（天神本紀）</ref>{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}、[[君 (カバネ)|君]]{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}を[[姓]]に持つ[[氏族]]とされる。
[[日本神話]]において天宇受売命が[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998|}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。この名前は、天宇受売命が[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定される{{要出典|date=2022年3月}}{{なぜ|date=2022年3月}}が、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]][[稗田村]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
== 考証 == {{要出典範囲|他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く|date=2021年5月}}、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。
=== 異説 === 「蓋し神代記紀の猿女の話は神話に過ぎじ、小野氏が猿女を貢するは反って相当の理由ありしか」という意見もある{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。これを受けて、宝賀寿男は、猿女の養田の所在地が[[近江国]]和邇村、[[山城国]]小野郷であることからも、和邇氏族の小野臣・和邇部臣両氏こそが主として猿女を輩出してきた氏族であると主張した。この説では、本来は[[猿田彦命]]・[[天宇受売命]]の後裔であった和邇氏族が、[[孝安天皇]]後裔の[[皇別]]氏族という系譜に変更されたことによって、猿女供出氏族ではないと主張したものとされる<ref>宝賀寿男「猿女君の意義 稗田阿禮の周辺（上）」『東アジアの古代文化』106号収録、[[大和書房]]、2001年、177-178頁。</ref>。
宝賀寿男は、「君・公」は姓ではなく女性への尊称であり、また『[[新撰姓氏録]]』などに猿女君について何ら記録がないこと、女性を始祖とする具体的な氏族の存在が確認できない{{要出典|date=2022年3月}}ことなどから、実際には猿女君という氏族は存在せず、女官の称号であったとする説を提唱した<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/kojikijo/jobunkou1.htm 稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文]」『古樹紀之房間』、2015年。</ref>。
ただし、『[[播磨国風土記]]』に記録されている、古里賣を始祖とする大部造や、他田熊千を始祖とする私部など、多くの氏族が『新撰姓氏録』には記されておらず、また、同じく『新撰姓氏録』には「山都多祁流比女命」という女神あるいは女性を祖とする[[摂津国]]の阿刀部氏の存在が記録されている。

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ・'''猨女君'''、'''猿女公'''）は、古代より[[朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきたとされる一族。
== 概要 == [[天神]]・[[天宇受売命]]を始祖としており<ref>『[[古事記]]』、『[[日本書紀]]』、『[[古語拾遺]]』、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』（天神本紀）</ref>{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}、[[君 (カバネ)|君]]{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}を[[姓]]に持つ[[氏族]]とされる。
[[日本神話]]において天宇受売命が[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998|}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。この名前は、天宇受売命が[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定される{{要出典|date=2022年3月}}{{なぜ|date=2022年3月}}が、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]][[稗田村]]（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
なお、『[[政事要略]]』巻八十四糺弾事二十四「伊賀国百姓解申進雑愁文事」には「右少史猿女副雄」という男性の官人や名前が記されている<ref>中野謙一「稗田阿礼は何をしたのか ― 修史事業における『古事記』の位置づけ―-」『愛知淑徳大学論集―文学部・文学研究科篇 ― 第三十七号 二〇一二・三一― 一二』[https://aska-r.repo.nii.ac.jp/index.php?action=repository_action_common_download&item_id=5750&item_no=1&attribute_id=12&file_no=1&page_id=37&block_id=59]</ref>。
== 考証 == {{要出典範囲|他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く|date=2021年5月}}、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。
=== 異説 === 「蓋し神代記紀の猿女の話は神話に過ぎじ、小野氏が猿女を貢するは反って相当の理由ありしか」という意見もある{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。
実際は猿女君という氏族は存在せず、女官の称号であったとする説が存在するが<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/kojikijo/jobunkou1.htm 稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文]」『古樹紀之房間』、2015年。</ref>、前述のように「右少史猿女副雄」という官人が確認できるため、この説は成り立たない<ref>中野謙一「稗田阿礼は何をしたのか ― 修史事業における『古事記』の位置づけ―-」『愛知淑徳大学論集―文学部・文学研究科篇 ― 第三十七号 二〇一二・三一― 一二』[https://aska-r.repo.nii.ac.jp/index.php?action=repository_action_common_download&item_id=5750&item_no=1&attribute_id=12&file_no=1&page_id=37&block_id=59]</ref>。
== 脚注 == <!--===注釈===--> {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Notelist}} <!--===出典===--> {{Reflist}}
== 参考文献 == * {{オープンアクセス}}{{Citation|和書|last=太田|first=亮|author-link=太田亮|others=[[上田萬年]]、[[三上参次]]監修|chapter=猿女 サルメ サメ|pages=2714-2715|volume=第2|date=1934|title=姓氏家系大辞典|publisher=姓氏家系大辞典刊行会|id={{全国書誌番号|47004572}}|chapter-url={{NDLDC|1130938/451}} 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション|ncid=BN05000207|oclc=673726070|ref=harv}} * {{Citation|和書|editor-last=佐伯|editor-first=有清|editor-link=佐伯有清|date=1994-11|title=日本古代氏族事典|publisher=[[雄山閣|雄山閣出版]]|isbn=4639012500|ncid=BN11610905|ref=harv}} * {{Cite web|author=株式会社日立ソリューションズ・クリエイト|date=1998-10|title=世界大百科事典内の猿女／猨女の言及|work = 世界大百科事典 第2版|publisher = [[コトバンク]] | url = https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%8C%BF%E5%A5%B3-512570|accessdate=2017-06-26|ref={{SfnRef|コトバンク|1998}}}} == 関連項目 == * [[巫女舞]] * [[鎮魂祭]]

[[日本神話]]において天宇受売命が[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。この名前は、天宇受売命が[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定される{{要出典|date=2022年3月}}{{なぜ|date=2022年3月}}が、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]]稗田村（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
なお、『[[政事要略]]』巻八十四糺弾事二十四「伊賀国百姓解申進雑愁文事」には「右少史猿女副雄」という男性の官人や名前が記されている<ref name="中野謙一">{{Cite journal|和書|author=中野謙一 |date=2012-03 |title=稗田阿礼は何をしたのか : 修史事業における『古事記』の位置づけ |journal=愛知淑徳大学論集. 文学部・文学研究科篇 |ISSN=1349-5496 |publisher=愛知淑徳大学文学部 |volume=37 |pages=1-12 |url=https://hdl.handle.net/10638/5085}}</ref>。
== 考証 == {{要出典範囲|他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く|date=2021年5月}}、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。
=== 異説 === 「蓋し神代記紀の猿女の話は神話に過ぎじ、小野氏が猿女を貢するは反って相当の理由ありしか」という意見もある{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。
実際は猿女君という氏族は存在せず、女官の称号であったとする説が存在するが<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/kojikijo/jobunkou1.htm 稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文]」『古樹紀之房間』、2015年。</ref>、前述のように「右少史猿女副雄」という官人が確認できるため、この説は成り立たない<ref name="中野謙一"/>。

revision.text:
The Sarume clan is a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. Together, [[Ame-no-Uzume]] and [[Sarutahiko Ōkami]] founded the [[Sarume clan]].<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" />
They are said to have interbred with the [[Wani clan]]<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Akima |first=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929 |journal=Japan Review |issue=4 |pages=141–198 |issn=0915-0986}}</ref>
The Wani clan is believed to be related to [[Wani (dragon)|Wani dragons]], with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal |last=Akima |first=Toshio |date=1993 |title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami |url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929 |journal=Japan Review |issue=4 |pages=141–198 |issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} They had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|ja|猿女君}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|ja|猿女君}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|ja|猿女君}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} [[ja:猿女君]] == Uzume and Sarutahiko == [[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb]] Amaterasu orders Uzume to accompany her grandson [[Ninigi]] on his journey to earth. They head to ''[[Ame-no-ukihashi]]'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they are blocked by [[Sarutahiko Ōkami|Sarutahiko]]. Uzume comes and persuades Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.
Later, [[Uzume]] and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|ja|猿女君}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>
== Worship == [[File:AmanoiwatoTablet.jpg|left|thumb|254x254px|Tablet at the Ama-no-Uzume shrine in [[Takachiho, Miyazaki|Takachiho]]]] Ame-no-Uzume-no-Mikoto is still worshiped today as a [[Shinto]] [[kami]], spirits indigenous to Japan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tsubaki Sukeikai |url=http://www.tsubakishrine.org/contact/TsubakiKoApplication2.pdf |access-date=23 August 2012 |publisher=Tsubaki Grand Shrine of America}}{{dead link|date=December 2017|bot=InternetArchiveBot|fix-attempted=yes}}</ref>
There are many shrines dedicated to the goddess including Chiyo shrine, [[Tsubaki Grand Shrine of America|Tsubaki America Shrine]] and [[Tsubaki Grand Shrine]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tsubaki Grand Shrine of America |url=http://www.tsubakishrine.org/history/index.html |access-date=Nov 23, 2020 |website=www.tsubakishrine.org}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=5 September 2017 |title=Chiyo Shrine |url=https://visit.hikoneshi.com/en/plan_your_visit/sightseeing/temples-shrines/chiyo-shrine/ |access-date=Nov 23, 2020 |website=Hikone Travel Guide}}</ref>
[[Category:{{draft categories|[[Category:Japan]] Wikipedia drafts[[Category:Japanese clans]] }}]] [[en:Draft:Sarume clan]] {{Sarutahiko Faith}}

[[日本神話]]において天宇受売命が[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。この名前は、天宇受売命が[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定される{{要出典|date=2022年3月}}{{なぜ|date=2022年3月}}が、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]]稗田村（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
なお、『[[政事要略]]』巻八十四糺弾事二十四「伊賀国百姓解申進雑愁文事」には「右少史猿女副雄」という男性の官人や名前が記されている<ref name="中野謙一">{{Cite journal|和書|author=中野謙一 |date=2012-03 |title=稗田阿礼は何をしたのか : 修史事業における『古事記』の位置づけ |journal=愛知淑徳大学論集. 文学部・文学研究科篇 |ISSN=1349-5496 |publisher=愛知淑徳大学文学部 |volume=37 |pages=1-12 |url=https://hdl.handle.net/10638/5085}}</ref>。
== 考証 == {{要出典範囲|他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く|date=2021年5月}}、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。
=== 異説 === 「蓋し神代記紀の猿女の話は神話に過ぎじ、小野氏が猿女を貢するは反って相当の理由ありしか」という意見もある{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。
実際は猿女君という氏族は存在せず、女官の称号であったとする説が存在するが<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/kojikijo/jobunkou1.htm 稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文]」『古樹紀之房間』、2015年。</ref>、前述のように「右少史猿女副雄」という官人が確認できるため、この説は成り立たない<ref name="中野謙一"/>。
== 脚注 == <!--===注釈===--> {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Notelist}} <!--===出典===--> {{Reflist}}
== 参考文献 == * {{オープンアクセス}}{{Citation|和書|last=太田|first=亮|author-link=太田亮|others=[[上田萬年]]、[[三上参次]]監修|chapter=猿女 サルメ サメ|pages=2714-2715|volume=第2|date=1934|title=姓氏家系大辞典|publisher=姓氏家系大辞典刊行会|id={{全国書誌番号|47004572}}|chapter-url={{NDLDC|1130938/451}} 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション|ncid=BN05000207|oclc=673726070|ref=harv}} * {{Citation|和書|editor-last=佐伯|editor-first=有清|editor-link=佐伯有清|date=1994-11|title=日本古代氏族事典|publisher=[[雄山閣|雄山閣出版]]|isbn=4639012500|ncid=BN11610905|ref=harv}} * {{Cite web|和書|author=株式会社日立ソリューションズ・クリエイト|date=1998-10|title=世界大百科事典内の猿女／猨女の言及|work = 世界大百科事典 第2版|publisher = [[コトバンク]] | url = https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%8C%BF%E5%A5%B3-512570|accessdate=2017-06-26|ref={{SfnRef|コトバンク|1998}}}}

'''猿女君'''（さるめのきみ・'''猨女君'''、'''猿女公'''）は、古代より[[朝廷 (日本)|朝廷]]の[[祭祀]]に携わってきたとされる一族。
== 概要 == [[天神]]・[[天宇受売命]]を始祖としており<ref>『[[古事記]]』、『[[日本書紀]]』、『[[古語拾遺]]』、『[[先代旧事本紀]]』（天神本紀）</ref>{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}、[[君 (カバネ)|君]]{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}を[[カバネ|姓]]に持つ[[氏族]]とされる。
[[日本神話]]において天宇受売命が[[天岩戸|岩戸隠れ]]の際に岩戸の前で[[舞]]を舞ったという伝承から、[[鎮魂|鎮魂祭]]での演舞や[[大嘗祭]]における前行などを執り行った[[猿女]]{{Sfn|コトバンク|1998}}を貢進した氏族とされる{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。この名前は、天宇受売命が[[天孫降臨]]の際に[[猿田毘古神]]と応対したことにより、猿田毘古神の名を残すために[[邇邇芸命]]より名づけられたものであると神話では説明している。実際には、「戯（さ）る女」の意味であると考えられている。
本拠地は[[伊勢国]]と想定される{{要出典|date=2022年3月}}{{なぜ|date=2022年3月}}が、一部は朝廷の祭祀を勤めるために、[[大和国]][[添上郡]]稗田村（現在の[[奈良県]][[大和郡山市]][[稗田町 (大和郡山市)|稗田町]]）に本拠地を移し、[[稗田氏]]を称した{{Sfn|佐伯|1994|p=247}}。
なお、『[[政事要略]]』巻八十四糺弾事二十四「伊賀国百姓解申進雑愁文事」には「右少史猿女副雄」という男性の官人や名前が記されている<ref name="中野謙一">{{Cite journal|和書|author=中野謙一 |date=2012-03 |title=稗田阿礼は何をしたのか : 修史事業における『古事記』の位置づけ |journal=愛知淑徳大学論集. 文学部・文学研究科篇 |ISSN=1349-5496 |publisher=愛知淑徳大学文学部 |volume=37 |pages=1-12 |url=https://hdl.handle.net/10638/5085}}</ref>。 また、[[須須神社]]の社家は現在でも「猿女」姓を名乗っている。
== 考証 == {{要出典範囲|他の祭祀氏族が男性が祭祀に携わっていたのに対し、猿女君は女性、すなわち[[巫女]]として祭祀に携わっていた。それ故に他の祭祀氏族よりも勢力が弱く|date=2021年5月}}、[[弘仁]]年間には[[小野氏]]・[[和邇氏|和邇部氏]]が猿女君の[[養田]]を横取りし、自分の子女を猿女君として貢進したということもあったともされる<ref>『[[類聚国史]]』巻19,猿女の条</ref>。
=== 異説 === 「蓋し神代記紀の猿女の話は神話に過ぎじ、小野氏が猿女を貢するは反って相当の理由ありしか」という意見もある{{Sfn|太田|1934|p=2715}}。
実際は猿女君という氏族は存在せず、女官の称号であったとする説が存在するが<ref>[[宝賀寿男]]「[http://wwr2.ucom.ne.jp/hetoyc15/kodaisi/kojikijo/jobunkou1.htm 稗田阿禮の実在性と古事記序文]」『古樹紀之房間』、2015年。</ref>、前述のように「右少史猿女副雄」という官人が確認できるため、この説は成り立たない<ref name="中野謙一"/>。
== 脚注 == <!--===注釈===--> {{脚注ヘルプ}} {{Notelist}} <!--===出典===--> {{Reflist}}
== 参考文献 == * {{オープンアクセス}}{{Citation|和書|last=太田|first=亮|author-link=太田亮|others=[[上田萬年]]、[[三上参次]]監修|chapter=猿女 サルメ サメ|pages=2714-2715|volume=第2|date=1934|title=姓氏家系大辞典|publisher=姓氏家系大辞典刊行会|id={{全国書誌番号|47004572}}|chapter-url={{NDLDC|1130938/451}} 国立国会図書館デジタルコレクション|ncid=BN05000207|oclc=673726070|ref=harv}} * {{Citation|和書|editor-last=佐伯|editor-first=有清|editor-link=佐伯有清|date=1994-11|title=日本古代氏族事典|publisher=[[雄山閣|雄山閣出版]]|isbn=4639012500|ncid=BN11610905|ref=harv}} * {{Cite web|和書|author=株式会社日立ソリューションズ・クリエイト|date=1998-10|title=世界大百科事典内の猿女／猨女の言及|work = 世界大百科事典 第2版|publisher = [[コトバンク]] | url = https://kotobank.jp/word/%E7%8C%BF%E5%A5%B3-512570|accessdate=2017-06-26|ref={{SfnRef|コトバンク|1998}}}}
== 関連項目 == * [[巫女舞]] * [[鎮魂祭]]

{{Infobox Japanese clan|province of origin=[[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]]|home province=[[:en:Ise Province|Ise Province]]|founder={{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}|image=File:Sarume Shrine.jpg|caption=Sarume shrine, a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine]], the traditional shrine of the family|image caption=Sarume shrine, a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine]], the traditional shrine of the family<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />
|alt=[[Sarutahiko Shrine]], the traditional shrine of the family}}

The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} was a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. They were founded by and descend from [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ama-no-Uzume]] and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, and are known for their female ritualists.<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム">{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9422|access-date=2024-03-18|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> They are sometimes identified with {{ill|Miko|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko|qq=}} or seen as their predecessors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kárpáti|first=János|date=2013|title=Music of Female Shamans in Japan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43290138|journal=Studia Musicologica|volume=54|issue=3|pages=225–256|issn=1788-6244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Averbuch|first=Irit|date=1998|title=Shamanic Dance in Japan: The Choreography of Possession in Kagura Performance|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1178756|journal=Asian Folklore Studies|volume=57|issue=2|pages=293–329|doi=10.2307/1178756|issn=0385-2342}}</ref> Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ge8cWl8OT3gC&pg=PA7&lpg=PA7&dq=sarume+miko&source=bl&ots=3-rirDOY9S&sig=ACfU3U2SXiNDAkXcLsQG-VAchhIu6H2z-A&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiqwd2xy_6EAxVJCTQIHX2kBrg4ChDoAXoECAIQAw#v=onepage&q=sarume%20miko&f=false|title=The Japanese Theatre: From Shamanistic Ritual to Contemporary Pluralism|last=Ortolani|first=Benito|date=1995|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-04333-3|language=en}}</ref>

There is a {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-31|title=Sarutahiko Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331032231/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarutahikojinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2022">{{Cite web|date=2022-12-01|title=Sarume Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201135853/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarumejinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-09|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209214747/https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp">{{Cite web|title=What is Sarutahiko-JinjaShrine Shrine and Sarume-JinjaShrine shrines where the strongest blessings reside that are essential for visiting Ise? {{!}} Interview report {{!}} Kanko Mie (Kanko Mie)|url=https://www.kankomie.or.jp/report/1556?wovn=en|access-date=2024-03-19|website=www.kankomie.or.jp|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} are known in Japanese mythology as descendants of Ame no Uzume, a deity celebrated for her pivotal role in the myth of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the sun goddess, retreating into the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (heavenly rock cave). .<ref name="hardacre-2017a">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|53-68}}

Sarume women were associated with {{ill|Kagura|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} dances being done during enthronement rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

In the [[Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] there was this organization.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} 

* The {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}} was responsible for managing the procuring materials for rituals and performing abstinence rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and distribution of tribute offerings within the Jingikan..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} claiming descent from Ame no [[Futodama|Futodama]] no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}
* {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} women were tasked with performing sacred dances..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} Initially serving as seers and healers, their role evolved to include performing ritual dances, or kagura, during Enthronement Rites and court ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} claiming descent from the goddess [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]] no Mikoto,<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. <ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" /> 
* The Tamatsukuri specialized in the creation of {{ill|Magatama|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Magatama|qq=}}..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
* The Kagamitsukuri were known for crafting {{ill|Mirrors in Shinto|lt=bronze mirrors|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mirrors in Shinto|qq=}} for use in shrine ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
* The {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} (卜部氏) considered to be of relatively low Rank, carried out divination practices..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9910|access-date=2024-03-19|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> using tortoise shells and deer [[:en:Scapula|scapulae]] <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}  later taking the surname {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} and claiming descent from {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft|qq=draft}} alongside the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]].<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

* [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]]: Later known as the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|lt=Fujiwara|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, they specialized in reciting prayers to the Kami, with a divine lineage tracing back to {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
''' In his book ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}} goes on to theorize that the {{Nihongo|[[:en:Ō clan|Ō clan]]|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]] who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken2">{{cite book|title=神道の本|last=小向|first=正司|publisher=学研|year=1992|series=Books Esoterica|volume=2|pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref>
''' Takemikazuchi was originally a local god (''kuni-tsu-kami'') revered by the {{Nihongo|[[:en:Ō clan|Ō clan]]|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}},<ref name="gakken2" /> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken2" /> However, the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]] who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami|ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}}<ref name="gakken2" />
All of these clans are descended from figures who played significant roles in the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin|3=en|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson korin|qq=}} and accompanied Ninigi during his descent, and many of them ({{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]], and {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}}) descend from figures ([[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]], [[Futodama]], {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} respectively) played roles in the myth of Amaterasu in the cave.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59}}

The {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} considered themselves excluded from this, and their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} was excluded. For this reason they wrote the {{ill|Kujiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujiki|qq=}}.  They were highly influential in the development of the department of divinities, but they were not a priestly clan. The Inbe felt their role was minimized so they wrote the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shui|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kogo Shui|qq=}} to improve their position too.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />

== History ==
[[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb|Sarutahiko and Ame no Uzume, the founders of the clan]]The tales tell of great rivalry between Amaterasu and Susano'o. When he was to leave [[:en:Heaven|Heaven]] forever because Izanagi ordered him to, he went to say goodbye to his sister. Amaterasu, suspicious, proposed him a challenge: each of them was to turn an object of the other's into people. Amaterasu created three women from Susanoo's sword while he created five men from her [[:en:Necklace|Necklace]]. Amaterasu said the men were hers because they were born of her necklace. Susano'o destroyed her [[:en:Rice|Rice]] fields, threw a dead [[:en:Pony|Pony]] into her [[:en:Loom|Loom]], and killed one of her assistants in [[:en:Anger|Anger]]. For this, Amaterasu, sad, angry and scared, went to hide inside [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]], the ''"heavenly rock [[:en:Cave|Cave]]"'', so the Sun was hidden and the world became dark for a long time. The [[:en:Oni (folklore)|Oni]] ([[:en:Devil|devils]] of Japanese mythology) came out to the dark world, and the gods could not make Amaterasu come out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

The intelligent goddess of [[:en:Happiness|Happiness]], [[Ame-no-Uzume]] (天宇受売命), took a big bucket, turned it upside down near the cave entrance, and began a dance on it, tearing off her clothing in front of the other Kami. They thought this was so funny that they laughed happily..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

Amaterasu heard them, and looked out to see why the gods were laughing. When she opened the cave, she saw her wonderful reflection in a [[:en:Mirror|Mirror]] Uzume had put on a tree, and slowly came out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

In Ancient times Amaterasu ordered Uzume to accompany her grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his journey to earth. They headed to ''{{ill|Ame-no-ukihashi|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-ukihashi|qq=}}'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they were blocked by {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. Uzume came and persuaded Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.

Later, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|lt=Uzume|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>

The Kogo Shui says that this is the origin of a rite done by the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

The Kojiki says that during her time in Ise, Uzume ensured the fish pledged their allegiance to Ninigi. The {{ill|sea cucumber|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sea cucumber|qq=}}, lacking a mouth, was unable to speak, so Uzume cut a mouth for it. This narrative depicts the Sarume no kimi as the initial recipients of offerings at Ise.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

Later in their history they are said to have interbred with the {{ill|Wani clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref> Which is believed to be related to {{ill|Wani (dragon)|lt=Wani dragons|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani (dragon)|qq=}}, with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} The wani clan had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the Sarume disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995" />

[[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] in Ise is linked to the same founding myth. The priests of the shrine are said to also be descendants of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2023-10-21|website=www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp}}</ref> who it worships.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-22|title=Sarutahiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122143817/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-date=2022-01-22|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>

There is a Sarume shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />

The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} was a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. They were founded by and descend from [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ama-no-Uzume]] and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, and are known for their female ritualists.<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム">{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9422|access-date=2024-03-18|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> They are sometimes identified with {{ill|Miko|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko|qq=}} or seen as their predecessors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kárpáti|first=János|date=2013|title=Music of Female Shamans in Japan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43290138|journal=Studia Musicologica|volume=54|issue=3|pages=225–256|issn=1788-6244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Averbuch|first=Irit|date=1998|title=Shamanic Dance in Japan: The Choreography of Possession in Kagura Performance|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1178756|journal=Asian Folklore Studies|volume=57|issue=2|pages=293–329|doi=10.2307/1178756|issn=0385-2342}}</ref> Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ge8cWl8OT3gC&pg=PA7&lpg=PA7&dq=sarume+miko&source=bl&ots=3-rirDOY9S&sig=ACfU3U2SXiNDAkXcLsQG-VAchhIu6H2z-A&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiqwd2xy_6EAxVJCTQIHX2kBrg4ChDoAXoECAIQAw#v=onepage&q=sarume%20miko&f=false|title=The Japanese Theatre: From Shamanistic Ritual to Contemporary Pluralism|last=Ortolani|first=Benito|date=1995|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-04333-3|language=en}}</ref>

There is a {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-31|title=Sarutahiko Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331032231/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarutahikojinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2022">{{Cite web|date=2022-12-01|title=Sarume Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201135853/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarumejinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-09|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209214747/https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp">{{Cite web|title=What is Sarutahiko-JinjaShrine Shrine and Sarume-JinjaShrine shrines where the strongest blessings reside that are essential for visiting Ise? {{!}} Interview report {{!}} Kanko Mie (Kanko Mie)|url=https://www.kankomie.or.jp/report/1556?wovn=en|access-date=2024-03-19|website=www.kankomie.or.jp|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} are known in Japanese mythology as descendants of Ame no Uzume, a deity celebrated for her pivotal role in the myth of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the sun goddess, retreating into the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (heavenly rock cave). .<ref name="hardacre-2017a">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|53-68}}

Sarume women were associated with {{ill|Kagura|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} dances being done during enthronement rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

In the [[Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] there was this organization.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} 

* The {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}} was responsible for managing the procuring materials for rituals and performing abstinence rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and distribution of tribute offerings within the Jingikan..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} claiming descent from Ame no [[Futodama|Futodama]] no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}
* {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} women were tasked with performing sacred dances..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} Initially serving as seers and healers, their role evolved to include performing ritual dances, or kagura, during Enthronement Rites and court ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} claiming descent from the goddess [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]] no Mikoto,<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. <ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" /> 
* The Tamatsukuri specialized in the creation of {{ill|Magatama|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Magatama|qq=}}..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
* The Kagamitsukuri were known for crafting {{ill|Mirrors in Shinto|lt=bronze mirrors|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mirrors in Shinto|qq=}} for use in shrine ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
* The {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} (卜部氏) considered to be of relatively low Rank, carried out divination practices..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9910|access-date=2024-03-19|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> using tortoise shells and deer [[:en:Scapula|scapulae]] <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}  later taking the surname {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} and claiming descent from {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft|qq=draft}} alongside the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]].<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

* [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]]: Later known as the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|lt=Fujiwara|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, they specialized in reciting prayers to the Kami, with a divine lineage tracing back to {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft|qq=draft}}
''' In his book ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}} goes on to theorize that the {{Nihongo|[[:en:Ō clan|Ō clan]]|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]] who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken2">{{cite book|title=神道の本|last=小向|first=正司|publisher=学研|year=1992|series=Books Esoterica|volume=2|pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref>
''' Takemikazuchi was originally a local god (''kuni-tsu-kami'') revered by the {{Nihongo|[[:en:Ō clan|Ō clan]]|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}},<ref name="gakken2" /> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken2" /> However, the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]] who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami|ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}}<ref name="gakken2" />
All of these clans are descended from figures who played significant roles in the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin|3=en|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson korin|qq=}} and accompanied Ninigi during his descent, and many of them ({{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]], and {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}}) descend from figures ([[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]], [[Futodama]], {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} respectively) played roles in the myth of Amaterasu in the cave.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59}}

The {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} considered themselves excluded from this, and their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} was excluded. For this reason they wrote the {{ill|Kujiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujiki|qq=}}.  They were highly influential in the development of the department of divinities, but they were not a priestly clan. The Inbe felt their role was minimized so they wrote the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shui|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kogo Shui|qq=}} to improve their position too.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />

== History ==
[[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb|Sarutahiko and Ame no Uzume, the founders of the clan]]The tales tell of great rivalry between Amaterasu and Susano'o. When he was to leave [[:en:Heaven|Heaven]] forever because Izanagi ordered him to, he went to say goodbye to his sister. Amaterasu, suspicious, proposed him a challenge: each of them was to turn an object of the other's into people. Amaterasu created three women from Susanoo's sword while he created five men from her [[:en:Necklace|Necklace]]. Amaterasu said the men were hers because they were born of her necklace. Susano'o destroyed her [[:en:Rice|Rice]] fields, threw a dead [[:en:Pony|Pony]] into her [[:en:Loom|Loom]], and killed one of her assistants in [[:en:Anger|Anger]]. For this, Amaterasu, sad, angry and scared, went to hide inside [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]], the ''"heavenly rock [[:en:Cave|Cave]]"'', so the Sun was hidden and the world became dark for a long time. The [[:en:Oni (folklore)|Oni]] ([[:en:Devil|devils]] of Japanese mythology) came out to the dark world, and the gods could not make Amaterasu come out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

The intelligent goddess of [[:en:Happiness|Happiness]], [[Ame-no-Uzume]] (天宇受売命), took a big bucket, turned it upside down near the cave entrance, and began a dance on it, tearing off her clothing in front of the other Kami. They thought this was so funny that they laughed happily..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

Amaterasu heard them, and looked out to see why the gods were laughing. When she opened the cave, she saw her wonderful reflection in a [[:en:Mirror|Mirror]] Uzume had put on a tree, and slowly came out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

In Ancient times Amaterasu ordered Uzume to accompany her grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his journey to earth. They headed to ''{{ill|Ame-no-ukihashi|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-ukihashi|qq=}}'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they were blocked by {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. Uzume came and persuaded Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.

Later, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|lt=Uzume|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>

The Kogo Shui says that this is the origin of a rite done by the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

The Kojiki says that during her time in Ise, Uzume ensured the fish pledged their allegiance to Ninigi. The {{ill|sea cucumber|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sea cucumber|qq=}}, lacking a mouth, was unable to speak, so Uzume cut a mouth for it. This narrative depicts the Sarume no kimi as the initial recipients of offerings at Ise.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

Later in their history they are said to have interbred with the {{ill|Wani clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref> Which is believed to be related to {{ill|Wani (dragon)|lt=Wani dragons|en|simple|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani (dragon)|qq=}}, with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} The wani clan had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the Sarume disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995" />

[[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] in Ise is linked to the same founding myth. The priests of the shrine are said to also be descendants of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2023-10-21|website=www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp}}</ref> who it worships.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-22|title=Sarutahiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122143817/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-date=2022-01-22|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>

There is a Sarume shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />

The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} was a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. They were founded by and descend from [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ama-no-Uzume]] and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, and are known for their female ritualists.<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム">{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9422|access-date=2024-03-18|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> They are sometimes identified with {{ill|Miko|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko|qq=}} or seen as their predecessors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kárpáti|first=János|date=2013|title=Music of Female Shamans in Japan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43290138|journal=Studia Musicologica|volume=54|issue=3|pages=225–256|issn=1788-6244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Averbuch|first=Irit|date=1998|title=Shamanic Dance in Japan: The Choreography of Possession in Kagura Performance|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1178756|journal=Asian Folklore Studies|volume=57|issue=2|pages=293–329|doi=10.2307/1178756|issn=0385-2342}}</ref> Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ge8cWl8OT3gC&pg=PA7&lpg=PA7&dq=sarume+miko&source=bl&ots=3-rirDOY9S&sig=ACfU3U2SXiNDAkXcLsQG-VAchhIu6H2z-A&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiqwd2xy_6EAxVJCTQIHX2kBrg4ChDoAXoECAIQAw#v=onepage&q=sarume%20miko&f=false|title=The Japanese Theatre: From Shamanistic Ritual to Contemporary Pluralism|last=Ortolani|first=Benito|date=1995|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-04333-3|language=en}}</ref>

There is a {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-31|title=Sarutahiko Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331032231/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarutahikojinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2022">{{Cite web|date=2022-12-01|title=Sarume Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201135853/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarumejinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-09|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209214747/https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp">{{Cite web|title=What is Sarutahiko-JinjaShrine Shrine and Sarume-JinjaShrine shrines where the strongest blessings reside that are essential for visiting Ise? {{!}} Interview report {{!}} Kanko Mie (Kanko Mie)|url=https://www.kankomie.or.jp/report/1556?wovn=en|access-date=2024-03-19|website=www.kankomie.or.jp|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} are known in Japanese mythology as descendants of Ame no Uzume, a deity celebrated for her pivotal role in the myth of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the sun goddess, retreating into the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (heavenly rock cave). .<ref name="hardacre-2017a">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|53-68}}

Sarume women were associated with {{ill|Kagura|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} dances being done during enthronement rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

In the [[Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] there was this organization.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} 

* The {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}} was responsible for managing the procuring materials for rituals and performing abstinence rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and distribution of tribute offerings within the Jingikan..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} claiming descent from Ame no [[Futodama|Futodama]] no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}
* {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} women were tasked with performing sacred dances..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} Initially serving as seers and healers, their role evolved to include performing ritual dances, or kagura, during Enthronement Rites and court ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} claiming descent from the goddess [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]] no Mikoto,<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. <ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" /> 
* The Tamatsukuri specialized in the creation of {{ill|Magatama|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Magatama|qq=}}..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The Kagamitsukuri were known for crafting {{ill|Mirrors in Shinto|lt=bronze mirrors|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mirrors in Shinto|qq=}} for use in shrine ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} (卜部氏) considered to be of relatively low Rank, carried out divination practices..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9910|access-date=2024-03-19|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> using tortoise shells and deer [[:en:Scapula|scapulae]] <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}  later taking the surname {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} and claiming descent from {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}} alongside the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]].<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

* [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]]: Later known as the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|lt=Fujiwara|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, they specialized in reciting prayers to the Kami, with a divine lineage tracing back to {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}}
''' In his book ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}} goes on to theorize that the {{Nihongo|[[:en:Ō clan|Ō clan]]|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]] who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken2">{{cite book|title=神道の本|last=小向|first=正司|publisher=学研|year=1992|series=Books Esoterica|volume=2|pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref>
''' Takemikazuchi was originally a local god (''kuni-tsu-kami'') revered by the {{Nihongo|[[:en:Ō clan|Ō clan]]|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}},<ref name="gakken2" /> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken2" /> However, the [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]] who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami|ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}}<ref name="gakken2" />
All of these clans are descended from figures who played significant roles in the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin|3=en|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson korin|qq=}} and accompanied Ninigi during his descent, and many of them ({{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}}, [[:en:Nakatomi clan|Nakatomi clan]], and {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}}) descend from figures ([[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]], [[Futodama]], {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} respectively) played roles in the myth of Amaterasu in the cave.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59}}

The {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} considered themselves excluded from this, and their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} was excluded. For this reason they wrote the {{ill|Kujiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujiki|qq=}}.  They were highly influential in the development of the department of divinities, but they were not a priestly clan. The Inbe felt their role was minimized so they wrote the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shui|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kogo Shui|qq=}} to improve their position too.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />

== History ==
[[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb|Sarutahiko and Ame no Uzume, the founders of the clan]]The tales tell of great rivalry between Amaterasu and Susano'o. When he was to leave [[:en:Heaven|Heaven]] forever because Izanagi ordered him to, he went to say goodbye to his sister. Amaterasu, suspicious, proposed him a challenge: each of them was to turn an object of the other's into people. Amaterasu created three women from Susanoo's sword while he created five men from her [[:en:Necklace|Necklace]]. Amaterasu said the men were hers because they were born of her necklace. Susano'o destroyed her [[:en:Rice|Rice]] fields, threw a dead [[:en:Pony|Pony]] into her [[:en:Loom|Loom]], and killed one of her assistants in [[:en:Anger|Anger]]. For this, Amaterasu, sad, angry and scared, went to hide inside [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]], the ''"heavenly rock [[:en:Cave|Cave]]"'', so the Sun was hidden and the world became dark for a long time. The [[:en:Oni (folklore)|Oni]] ([[:en:Devil|devils]] of Japanese mythology) came out to the dark world, and the gods could not make Amaterasu come out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

The intelligent goddess of [[:en:Happiness|Happiness]], [[Ame-no-Uzume]] (天宇受売命), took a big bucket, turned it upside down near the cave entrance, and began a dance on it, tearing off her clothing in front of the other Kami. They thought this was so funny that they laughed happily..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

Amaterasu heard them, and looked out to see why the gods were laughing. When she opened the cave, she saw her wonderful reflection in a [[:en:Mirror|Mirror]] Uzume had put on a tree, and slowly came out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

In Ancient times Amaterasu ordered Uzume to accompany her grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his journey to earth. They headed to ''{{ill|Ame-no-ukihashi|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-ukihashi|qq=}}'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they were blocked by {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. Uzume came and persuaded Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.

Later, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|lt=Uzume|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>

The Kogo Shui says that this is the origin of a rite done by the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

The Kojiki says that during her time in Ise, Uzume ensured the fish pledged their allegiance to Ninigi. The {{ill|sea cucumber|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sea cucumber|qq=}}, lacking a mouth, was unable to speak, so Uzume cut a mouth for it. This narrative depicts the Sarume no kimi as the initial recipients of offerings at Ise.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

Later in their history they are said to have interbred with the {{ill|Wani clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref> Which is believed to be related to {{ill|Wani (dragon)|lt=Wani dragons|en|simple|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani (dragon)|qq=}}, with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} The wani clan had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the Sarume disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995" />

[[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] in Ise is linked to the same founding myth. The priests of the shrine are said to also be descendants of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|qq=draft|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2023-10-21|website=www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp}}</ref> who it worships.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-22|title=Sarutahiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122143817/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-date=2022-01-22|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>

There is a Sarume shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />
