The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} was a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. They were founded by and descend from [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ama-no-Uzume]] and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, and are known for their female ritualists.<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム">{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9422|access-date=2024-03-18|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> They are sometimes identified with {{ill|Miko|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko|qq=}} or seen as their predecessors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kárpáti|first=János|date=2013|title=Music of Female Shamans in Japan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43290138|journal=Studia Musicologica|volume=54|issue=3|pages=225–256|issn=1788-6244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Averbuch|first=Irit|date=1998|title=Shamanic Dance in Japan: The Choreography of Possession in Kagura Performance|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1178756|journal=Asian Folklore Studies|volume=57|issue=2|pages=293–329|doi=10.2307/1178756|issn=0385-2342}}</ref> Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ge8cWl8OT3gC&pg=PA7&lpg=PA7&dq=sarume+miko&source=bl&ots=3-rirDOY9S&sig=ACfU3U2SXiNDAkXcLsQG-VAchhIu6H2z-A&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiqwd2xy_6EAxVJCTQIHX2kBrg4ChDoAXoECAIQAw#v=onepage&q=sarume%20miko&f=false|title=The Japanese Theatre: From Shamanistic Ritual to Contemporary Pluralism|last=Ortolani|first=Benito|date=1995|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-04333-3|language=en}}</ref>

There is a {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-31|title=Sarutahiko Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331032231/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarutahikojinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2022">{{Cite web|date=2022-12-01|title=Sarume Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201135853/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarumejinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-09|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209214747/https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp">{{Cite web|title=What is Sarutahiko-JinjaShrine Shrine and Sarume-JinjaShrine shrines where the strongest blessings reside that are essential for visiting Ise? {{!}} Interview report {{!}} Kanko Mie (Kanko Mie)|url=https://www.kankomie.or.jp/report/1556?wovn=en|access-date=2024-03-19|website=www.kankomie.or.jp|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} are known in Japanese mythology as descendants of Ame no Uzume, a deity celebrated for her pivotal role in the myth of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the sun goddess, retreating into the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (heavenly rock cave). .<ref name="hardacre-2017a">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|53-68}}

Sarume women were associated with {{ill|Kagura|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} dances being done during enthronement rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

In the [[Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] there was this organization.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} 

* The {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}} was responsible for managing the procuring materials for rituals and performing abstinence rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and distribution of tribute offerings within the Jingikan..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} claiming descent from Ame no [[Futodama|Futodama]] no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}
* {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} women were tasked with performing sacred dances..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} Initially serving as seers and healers, their role evolved to include performing ritual dances, or kagura, during Enthronement Rites and court ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} claiming descent from the goddess [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]] no Mikoto,<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. <ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" /> 
* The Tamatsukuri specialized in the creation of {{ill|Magatama|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Magatama|qq=}}..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The Kagamitsukuri were known for crafting {{ill|Mirrors in Shinto|lt=bronze mirrors|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mirrors in Shinto|qq=}} for use in shrine ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} (卜部氏) considered to be of relatively low Rank, carried out divination practices..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9910|access-date=2024-03-19|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> using tortoise shells and deer {{ill|Scapula|en|Scapula|WD=Q16336|lt=scapulae}} <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}  later taking the surname {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} and claiming descent from {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}} alongside the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

* {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}: Later known as the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|lt=Fujiwara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, they specialized in reciting prayers to the Kami, with a divine lineage tracing back to {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}}
''' In his book ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}} goes on to theorize that the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}} who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken2">{{cite book|title=神道の本|last=小向|first=正司|publisher=学研|year=1992|series=Books Esoterica|volume=2|pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref>
''' Takemikazuchi was originally a local god (''kuni-tsu-kami'') revered by the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}},<ref name="gakken2" /> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken2" /> However, the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}} who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami|ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}}<ref name="gakken2" />
All of these clans are descended from figures who played significant roles in the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin|3=en|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson korin|qq=}} and accompanied Ninigi during his descent, and many of them ({{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}, and {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}}) descend from figures ([[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]], [[Futodama]], {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} respectively) played roles in the myth of Amaterasu in the cave.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59}}

The {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} considered themselves excluded from this, and their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} was excluded. For this reason they wrote the {{ill|Kujiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujiki|qq=}}.  They were highly influential in the development of the department of divinities, but they were not a priestly clan. The Inbe felt their role was minimized so they wrote the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shui|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kogo Shui|qq=}} to improve their position too.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />

== History ==
[[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb|Sarutahiko and Ame no Uzume, the founders of the clan]]The tales tell of great rivalry between Amaterasu and Susano'o. When he was to leave {{ill|Heaven|en|Heaven|WD=Q4489450|lt=Heaven}} forever because Izanagi ordered him to, he went to say goodbye to his sister. Amaterasu, suspicious, proposed him a challenge: each of them was to turn an object of the other's into people. Amaterasu created three women from Susanoo's sword while he created five men from her {{ill|Necklace|en|Necklace|WD=Q189299|lt=Necklace}}. Amaterasu said the men were hers because they were born of her necklace. Susano'o destroyed her {{ill|Rice|en|Rice|WD=Q5090|lt=Rice}} fields, threw a dead {{ill|Pony|en|Pony|WD=Q188828|lt=Pony}} into her {{ill|Loom|en|Loom|WD=Q173056|lt=Loom}}, and killed one of her assistants in {{ill|Anger|en|Anger|WD=Q79871|lt=Anger}}. For this, Amaterasu, sad, angry and scared, went to hide inside [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]], the ''"heavenly rock {{ill|Cave|en|Cave|WD=Q35509|lt=Cave}}"'', so the Sun was hidden and the world became dark for a long time. The [[:en:Oni (folklore)|Oni]] ({{ill|Devil|en|Devil|WD=Q6674|lt=devils}} of Japanese mythology) came out to the dark world, and the gods could not make Amaterasu come out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

The intelligent goddess of {{ill|Happiness|en|Happiness|WD=Q8|lt=Happiness}}, [[Ame-no-Uzume]] (天宇受売命), took a big bucket, turned it upside down near the cave entrance, and began a dance on it, tearing off her clothing in front of the other Kami. They thought this was so funny that they laughed happily..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

Amaterasu heard them, and looked out to see why the gods were laughing. When she opened the cave, she saw her wonderful reflection in a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|WD=Q35197|lt=Mirror}} Uzume had put on a tree, and slowly came out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

In Ancient times Amaterasu ordered Uzume to accompany her grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his journey to earth. They headed to ''{{ill|Ame-no-ukihashi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-ukihashi|qq=}}'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they were blocked by {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. Uzume came and persuaded Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.

Later, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|lt=Uzume|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>

The Kogo Shui says that this is the origin of a rite done by the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

The Kojiki says that during her time in Ise, Uzume ensured the fish pledged their allegiance to Ninigi. The {{ill|sea cucumber|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sea cucumber|qq=}}, lacking a mouth, was unable to speak, so Uzume cut a mouth for it. This narrative depicts the Sarume no kimi as the initial recipients of offerings at Ise.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

Later in their history they are said to have interbred with the {{ill|Wani clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref> Which is believed to be related to {{ill|Wani (dragon)|lt=Wani dragons|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani (dragon)|qq=}}, with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} The wani clan had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the Sarume disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995" />

[[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] in Ise is linked to the same founding myth. The priests of the shrine are said to also be descendants of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2023-10-21|website=www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp}}</ref> who it worships.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-22|title=Sarutahiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122143817/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-date=2022-01-22|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>

There is a Sarume shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />

|alt=[[Sarutahiko Shrine]], the traditional shrine of the family}}

The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} was a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. They were founded by and descend from [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ama-no-Uzume]] and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, and are known for their female ritualists.<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム">{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9422|access-date=2024-03-18|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> They are sometimes identified with {{ill|Miko|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko|qq=}} or seen as their predecessors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kárpáti|first=János|date=2013|title=Music of Female Shamans in Japan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43290138|journal=Studia Musicologica|volume=54|issue=3|pages=225–256|issn=1788-6244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Averbuch|first=Irit|date=1998|title=Shamanic Dance in Japan: The Choreography of Possession in Kagura Performance|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1178756|journal=Asian Folklore Studies|volume=57|issue=2|pages=293–329|doi=10.2307/1178756|issn=0385-2342}}</ref> Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ge8cWl8OT3gC&pg=PA7&lpg=PA7&dq=sarume+miko&source=bl&ots=3-rirDOY9S&sig=ACfU3U2SXiNDAkXcLsQG-VAchhIu6H2z-A&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiqwd2xy_6EAxVJCTQIHX2kBrg4ChDoAXoECAIQAw#v=onepage&q=sarume%20miko&f=false|title=The Japanese Theatre: From Shamanistic Ritual to Contemporary Pluralism|last=Ortolani|first=Benito|date=1995|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-04333-3|language=en}}</ref>

There is a {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-31|title=Sarutahiko Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331032231/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarutahikojinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2022">{{Cite web|date=2022-12-01|title=Sarume Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201135853/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarumejinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-09|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209214747/https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp">{{Cite web|title=What is Sarutahiko-JinjaShrine Shrine and Sarume-JinjaShrine shrines where the strongest blessings reside that are essential for visiting Ise? {{!}} Interview report {{!}} Kanko Mie (Kanko Mie)|url=https://www.kankomie.or.jp/report/1556?wovn=en|access-date=2024-03-19|website=www.kankomie.or.jp|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} are known in Japanese mythology as descendants of Ame no Uzume, a deity celebrated for her pivotal role in the myth of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the sun goddess, retreating into the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (heavenly rock cave). .<ref name="hardacre-2017a">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|53-68}}

Sarume women were associated with {{ill|Kagura|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} dances being done during enthronement rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

In the [[Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] there was this organization.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} 

* The {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}} was responsible for managing the procuring materials for rituals and performing abstinence rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and distribution of tribute offerings within the Jingikan..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} claiming descent from Ame no [[Futodama|Futodama]] no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}
* {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} women were tasked with performing sacred dances..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} Initially serving as seers and healers, their role evolved to include performing ritual dances, or kagura, during Enthronement Rites and court ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} claiming descent from the goddess [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]] no Mikoto,<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. <ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" /> 
* The Tamatsukuri specialized in the creation of {{ill|Magatama|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Magatama|qq=}}..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The Kagamitsukuri were known for crafting {{ill|Mirrors in Shinto|lt=bronze mirrors|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mirrors in Shinto|qq=}} for use in shrine ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} (卜部氏) considered to be of relatively low Rank, carried out divination practices..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9910|access-date=2024-03-19|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> using tortoise shells and deer {{ill|Scapula|en|Scapula|WD=Q16336|lt=scapulae}} <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}  later taking the surname {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} and claiming descent from {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}} alongside the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

* {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}: Later known as the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|lt=Fujiwara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, they specialized in reciting prayers to the Kami, with a divine lineage tracing back to {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}}
''' In his book ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}} goes on to theorize that the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}} who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken2">{{cite book|title=神道の本|last=小向|first=正司|publisher=学研|year=1992|series=Books Esoterica|volume=2|pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref>
''' Takemikazuchi was originally a local god (''kuni-tsu-kami'') revered by the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}},<ref name="gakken2" /> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken2" /> However, the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}} who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami|ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}}<ref name="gakken2" />
All of these clans are descended from figures who played significant roles in the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin|3=en|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson korin|qq=}} and accompanied Ninigi during his descent, and many of them ({{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}, and {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}}) descend from figures ([[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]], [[Futodama]], {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} respectively) played roles in the myth of Amaterasu in the cave.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59}}

The {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} considered themselves excluded from this, and their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} was excluded. For this reason they wrote the {{ill|Kujiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujiki|qq=}}.  They were highly influential in the development of the department of divinities, but they were not a priestly clan. The Inbe felt their role was minimized so they wrote the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shui|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kogo Shui|qq=}} to improve their position too.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />

== History ==
[[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb|Sarutahiko and Ame no Uzume, the founders of the clan]]The tales tell of great rivalry between Amaterasu and Susano'o. When he was to leave {{ill|Heaven|en|Heaven|WD=Q4489450|lt=Heaven}} forever because Izanagi ordered him to, he went to say goodbye to his sister. Amaterasu, suspicious, proposed him a challenge: each of them was to turn an object of the other's into people. Amaterasu created three women from Susanoo's sword while he created five men from her {{ill|Necklace|en|Necklace|WD=Q189299|lt=Necklace}}. Amaterasu said the men were hers because they were born of her necklace. Susano'o destroyed her {{ill|Rice|en|Rice|WD=Q5090|lt=Rice}} fields, threw a dead {{ill|Pony|en|Pony|WD=Q188828|lt=Pony}} into her {{ill|Loom|en|Loom|WD=Q173056|lt=Loom}}, and killed one of her assistants in {{ill|Anger|en|Anger|WD=Q79871|lt=Anger}}. For this, Amaterasu, sad, angry and scared, went to hide inside [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]], the ''"heavenly rock {{ill|Cave|en|Cave|WD=Q35509|lt=Cave}}"'', so the Sun was hidden and the world became dark for a long time. The [[:en:Oni (folklore)|Oni]] ({{ill|Devil|en|Devil|WD=Q6674|lt=devils}} of Japanese mythology) came out to the dark world, and the gods could not make Amaterasu come out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

The intelligent goddess of {{ill|Happiness|en|Happiness|WD=Q8|lt=Happiness}}, [[Ame-no-Uzume]] (天宇受売命), took a big bucket, turned it upside down near the cave entrance, and began a dance on it, tearing off her clothing in front of the other Kami. They thought this was so funny that they laughed happily..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

Amaterasu heard them, and looked out to see why the gods were laughing. When she opened the cave, she saw her wonderful reflection in a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|WD=Q35197|lt=Mirror}} Uzume had put on a tree, and slowly came out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

In Ancient times Amaterasu ordered Uzume to accompany her grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his journey to earth. They headed to ''{{ill|Ame-no-ukihashi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-ukihashi|qq=}}'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they were blocked by {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. Uzume came and persuaded Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.

Later, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|lt=Uzume|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>

The Kogo Shui says that this is the origin of a rite done by the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

The Kojiki says that during her time in Ise, Uzume ensured the fish pledged their allegiance to Ninigi. The {{ill|sea cucumber|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sea cucumber|qq=}}, lacking a mouth, was unable to speak, so Uzume cut a mouth for it. This narrative depicts the Sarume no kimi as the initial recipients of offerings at Ise.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

Later in their history they are said to have interbred with the {{ill|Wani clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref> Which is believed to be related to {{ill|Wani (dragon)|lt=Wani dragons|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani (dragon)|qq=}}, with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} The wani clan had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the Sarume disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995" />

[[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] in Ise is linked to the same founding myth. The priests of the shrine are said to also be descendants of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2023-10-21|website=www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp}}</ref> who it worships.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-22|title=Sarutahiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122143817/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-date=2022-01-22|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>

There is a Sarume shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />

The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} was a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. They were founded by and descend from [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ama-no-Uzume]] and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, and are known for their female ritualists.<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム">{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9422|access-date=2024-03-18|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> They are sometimes identified with {{ill|Miko|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko|qq=}} or seen as their predecessors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kárpáti|first=János|date=2013|title=Music of Female Shamans in Japan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43290138|journal=Studia Musicologica|volume=54|issue=3|pages=225–256|issn=1788-6244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Averbuch|first=Irit|date=1998|title=Shamanic Dance in Japan: The Choreography of Possession in Kagura Performance|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1178756|journal=Asian Folklore Studies|volume=57|issue=2|pages=293–329|doi=10.2307/1178756|issn=0385-2342}}</ref> Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ge8cWl8OT3gC&pg=PA7&lpg=PA7&dq=sarume+miko&source=bl&ots=3-rirDOY9S&sig=ACfU3U2SXiNDAkXcLsQG-VAchhIu6H2z-A&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiqwd2xy_6EAxVJCTQIHX2kBrg4ChDoAXoECAIQAw#v=onepage&q=sarume%20miko&f=false|title=The Japanese Theatre: From Shamanistic Ritual to Contemporary Pluralism|last=Ortolani|first=Benito|date=1995|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-04333-3|language=en}}</ref>

There is a {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-31|title=Sarutahiko Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331032231/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarutahikojinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2022">{{Cite web|date=2022-12-01|title=Sarume Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201135853/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarumejinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-09|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209214747/https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp">{{Cite web|title=What is Sarutahiko-JinjaShrine Shrine and Sarume-JinjaShrine shrines where the strongest blessings reside that are essential for visiting Ise? {{!}} Interview report {{!}} Kanko Mie (Kanko Mie)|url=https://www.kankomie.or.jp/report/1556?wovn=en|access-date=2024-03-19|website=www.kankomie.or.jp|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} are known in Japanese mythology as descendants of Ame no Uzume, a deity celebrated for her pivotal role in the myth of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the sun goddess, retreating into the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (heavenly rock cave). .<ref name="hardacre-2017a">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|53-68}}

Sarume women were associated with {{ill|Kagura|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} dances being done during enthronement rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

In the [[Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] there was this organization.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} 

* The {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}} was responsible for managing the procuring materials for rituals and performing abstinence rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and distribution of tribute offerings within the Jingikan..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} claiming descent from Ame no [[Futodama|Futodama]] no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}
* {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} women were tasked with performing sacred dances..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} Initially serving as seers and healers, their role evolved to include performing ritual dances, or kagura, during Enthronement Rites and court ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} claiming descent from the goddess [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]] no Mikoto,<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. <ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" /> 
* The Tamatsukuri specialized in the creation of {{ill|Magatama|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Magatama|qq=}}..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The Kagamitsukuri were known for crafting {{ill|Mirrors in Shinto|lt=bronze mirrors|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mirrors in Shinto|qq=}} for use in shrine ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} (卜部氏) considered to be of relatively low Rank, carried out divination practices..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9910|access-date=2024-03-19|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> using tortoise shells and deer {{ill|Scapula|en|Scapula|WD=Q16336|lt=scapulae}} <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}  later taking the surname {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} and claiming descent from {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}} alongside the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

* {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}: Later known as the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|lt=Fujiwara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, they specialized in reciting prayers to the Kami, with a divine lineage tracing back to {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}}
''' In his book ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}} goes on to theorize that the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}} who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken2">{{cite book|title=神道の本|last=小向|first=正司|publisher=学研|year=1992|series=Books Esoterica|volume=2|pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref>
''' Takemikazuchi was originally a local god (''kuni-tsu-kami'') revered by the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}},<ref name="gakken2" /> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken2" /> However, the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}} who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami|ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}}<ref name="gakken2" />
All of these clans are descended from figures who played significant roles in the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin|3=en|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson korin|qq=}} and accompanied Ninigi during his descent, and many of them ({{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan}}, and {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}}) descend from figures ([[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]], [[Futodama]], {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} respectively) played roles in the myth of Amaterasu in the cave.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59}}

The {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} considered themselves excluded from this, and their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} was excluded. For this reason they wrote the {{ill|Kujiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujiki|qq=}}.  They were highly influential in the development of the department of divinities, but they were not a priestly clan. The Inbe felt their role was minimized so they wrote the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shui|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kogo Shui|qq=}} to improve their position too.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />

== History ==
[[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb|Sarutahiko and Ame no Uzume, the founders of the clan]]The tales tell of great rivalry between Amaterasu and Susano'o. When he was to leave {{ill|Heaven|en|Heaven|WD=Q4489450|lt=Heaven}} forever because Izanagi ordered him to, he went to say goodbye to his sister. Amaterasu, suspicious, proposed him a challenge: each of them was to turn an object of the other's into people. Amaterasu created three women from Susanoo's sword while he created five men from her {{ill|Necklace|en|Necklace|WD=Q189299|lt=Necklace}}. Amaterasu said the men were hers because they were born of her necklace. Susano'o destroyed her {{ill|Rice|en|Rice|WD=Q5090|lt=Rice}} fields, threw a dead {{ill|Pony|en|Pony|WD=Q188828|lt=Pony}} into her {{ill|Loom|en|Loom|WD=Q173056|lt=Loom}}, and killed one of her assistants in {{ill|Anger|en|Anger|WD=Q79871|lt=Anger}}. For this, Amaterasu, sad, angry and scared, went to hide inside [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]], the ''"heavenly rock {{ill|Cave|en|Cave|WD=Q35509|lt=Cave}}"'', so the Sun was hidden and the world became dark for a long time. The [[:en:Oni (folklore)|Oni]] ({{ill|Devil|en|Devil|WD=Q6674|lt=devils}} of Japanese mythology) came out to the dark world, and the gods could not make Amaterasu come out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

The intelligent goddess of {{ill|Happiness|en|Happiness|WD=Q8|lt=Happiness}}, [[Ame-no-Uzume]] (天宇受売命), took a big bucket, turned it upside down near the cave entrance, and began a dance on it, tearing off her clothing in front of the other Kami. They thought this was so funny that they laughed happily..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

Amaterasu heard them, and looked out to see why the gods were laughing. When she opened the cave, she saw her wonderful reflection in a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|WD=Q35197|lt=Mirror}} Uzume had put on a tree, and slowly came out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

In Ancient times Amaterasu ordered Uzume to accompany her grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his journey to earth. They headed to ''{{ill|Ame-no-ukihashi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-ukihashi|qq=}}'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they were blocked by {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. Uzume came and persuaded Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.

Later, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|lt=Uzume|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>

The Kogo Shui says that this is the origin of a rite done by the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

The Kojiki says that during her time in Ise, Uzume ensured the fish pledged their allegiance to Ninigi. The {{ill|sea cucumber|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sea cucumber|qq=}}, lacking a mouth, was unable to speak, so Uzume cut a mouth for it. This narrative depicts the Sarume no kimi as the initial recipients of offerings at Ise.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

Later in their history they are said to have interbred with the {{ill|Wani clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref> Which is believed to be related to {{ill|Wani (dragon)|lt=Wani dragons|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani (dragon)|qq=}}, with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} The wani clan had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the Sarume disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995" />

[[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] in Ise is linked to the same founding myth. The priests of the shrine are said to also be descendants of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2023-10-21|website=www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp}}</ref> who it worships.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-22|title=Sarutahiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122143817/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-date=2022-01-22|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>

There is a Sarume shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />

|alt=[[Sarutahiko Shrine]], the traditional shrine of the family}}

The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} was a Japanese clan<ref>{{Cite web |title=Sarume Clan • . A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |url=https://historyofjapan.co.uk/wiki/sarume-clan/ |access-date=2023-10-13 |website=. A History . . of Japan . 日本歴史 |language=en-GB}}</ref>. They were founded by and descend from [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ama-no-Uzume]] and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}, and are known for their female ritualists.<ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム">{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9422|access-date=2024-03-18|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> They are sometimes identified with {{ill|Miko|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Miko|qq=}} or seen as their predecessors.<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Kárpáti|first=János|date=2013|title=Music of Female Shamans in Japan|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/43290138|journal=Studia Musicologica|volume=54|issue=3|pages=225–256|issn=1788-6244}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last=Averbuch|first=Irit|date=1998|title=Shamanic Dance in Japan: The Choreography of Possession in Kagura Performance|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/1178756|journal=Asian Folklore Studies|volume=57|issue=2|pages=293–329|doi=10.2307/1178756|issn=0385-2342}}</ref> Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.ca/books?id=ge8cWl8OT3gC&pg=PA7&lpg=PA7&dq=sarume+miko&source=bl&ots=3-rirDOY9S&sig=ACfU3U2SXiNDAkXcLsQG-VAchhIu6H2z-A&hl=en&sa=X&ved=2ahUKEwiqwd2xy_6EAxVJCTQIHX2kBrg4ChDoAXoECAIQAw#v=onepage&q=sarume%20miko&f=false|title=The Japanese Theatre: From Shamanistic Ritual to Contemporary Pluralism|last=Ortolani|first=Benito|date=1995|publisher=Princeton University Press|isbn=978-0-691-04333-3|language=en}}</ref>

There is a {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a">{{Cite web|date=2023-03-31|title=Sarutahiko Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20230331032231/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarutahikojinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2022">{{Cite web|date=2022-12-01|title=Sarume Shrine {{!}} Ise City Tourism Association|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20221201135853/https://en.ise-kanko.jp/purpose/sarumejinja/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b">{{Cite web|date=2023-12-09|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231209214747/https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2024-03-19|website=web.archive.org}}</ref><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp">{{Cite web|title=What is Sarutahiko-JinjaShrine Shrine and Sarume-JinjaShrine shrines where the strongest blessings reside that are essential for visiting Ise? {{!}} Interview report {{!}} Kanko Mie (Kanko Mie)|url=https://www.kankomie.or.jp/report/1556?wovn=en|access-date=2024-03-19|website=www.kankomie.or.jp|language=en}}</ref>

== Overview ==
The {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} are known in Japanese mythology as descendants of Ame no Uzume, a deity celebrated for her pivotal role in the myth of [[Amaterasu|Amaterasu]], the sun goddess, retreating into the [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]] (heavenly rock cave). .<ref name="hardacre-2017a">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=_Q81DQAAQBAJ|title=Shinto: A History|last=Hardacre|first=Helen|date=2017|publisher=Oxford University Press|isbn=978-0-19-062171-1|language=en}}</ref>{{rp|53-68}}

Sarume women were associated with {{ill|Kagura|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kagura|qq=}} dances being done during enthronement rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

In the [[Department of Divinities|Department of Divinities]] there was this organization.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} 

* The {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}} was responsible for managing the procuring materials for rituals and performing abstinence rites.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and distribution of tribute offerings within the Jingikan..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} claiming descent from Ame no [[Futodama|Futodama]] no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}
* {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} women were tasked with performing sacred dances..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} Initially serving as seers and healers, their role evolved to include performing ritual dances, or kagura, during Enthronement Rites and court ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} claiming descent from the goddess [[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]] no Mikoto,<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}} and {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. <ref name="picken-2004a" /><ref name="roberts-2009a" /><ref name="coulter-2013a" /><ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" /> 
* The Tamatsukuri specialized in the creation of {{ill|Magatama|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Magatama|qq=}}..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tamanooya-no-Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The Kagamitsukuri were known for crafting {{ill|Mirrors in Shinto|lt=bronze mirrors|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mirrors in Shinto|qq=}} for use in shrine ceremonies..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}} and are descended from {{ill|Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ishikori-dome no Mikoto|qq=}}. <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59|qq=draft}}
* The {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} (卜部氏) considered to be of relatively low Rank, carried out divination practices..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|35}}<ref>{{Cite web|title=Encyclopedia of Shinto詳細|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/id=9910|access-date=2024-03-19|website=國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|language=ja}}</ref> using tortoise shells and deer {{ill|Scapula|en|Scapula|WD=Q16336|lt=scapulae|1=Scapula}} <ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}  later taking the surname {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Yoshida|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}} and claiming descent from {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}} alongside the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan|1=Nakatomi clan}}.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26}}

* {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan|1=Nakatomi clan}}: Later known as the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|lt=Fujiwara|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Fujiwara clan|qq=}}, they specialized in reciting prayers to the Kami, with a divine lineage tracing back to {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} no Mikoto..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|25-26|qq=draft}}
''' In his book ''Jinja to kodai ōken saishi'' (1989). {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}} goes on to theorize that the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan|1=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}} was originally {{Nihongo|ōmi|大忌|"greater taboo (priesthood)"}}, but was usurped by the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan|1=Nakatomi clan}} who were among the "lesser priesthood" (the latter claims descent from the {{Nihongo|[[Inbe clan]]|[[:ja:忌部氏|忌部氏]]}}).<ref name="gakken2">{{cite book|title=神道の本|last=小向|first=正司|publisher=学研|year=1992|series=Books Esoterica|volume=2|pages=76–7}}(zasshi code 66951-07; kyōtsu zasshi code T10-66951-07-1000)</ref>
''' Takemikazuchi was originally a local god (''kuni-tsu-kami'') revered by the {{Nihongo|{{ill|Ō clan|en|Ō clan|WD=Q11430816|lt=Ō clan|1=Ō clan}}|[[:ja:多氏|多氏]]|''Ō no uji''|extra=also written as {{Nihongo2|大氏}}}},<ref name="gakken2" /> and was a god of maritime travel.<ref name="gakken2" /> However, the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan|1=Nakatomi clan}} who also has roots in this region, and when they took over control of priestly duties from the Ō clan, they also instituted Takemikazuchi as the Nakatomi clan's [[ujigami|ujigami]] (clan deity). Or so this is the observation by {{ill|Iwao Ōwa|ja|大和岩雄|vertical-align=sup|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Iwao Ōwa|qq=}}<ref name="gakken2" />
All of these clans are descended from figures who played significant roles in the {{ill|Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson kōrin|lt=Tenson korin|3=en|4=en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Tenson korin|qq=}} and accompanied Ninigi during his descent, and many of them ({{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Inbe clan|Inbe family|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Inbe clan|qq=}}, {{ill|Nakatomi clan|en|Nakatomi clan|WD=Q1198447|lt=Nakatomi clan|1=Nakatomi clan}}, and {{ill|Urabe clan|lt=Urabe clan|lt=Yoshida family|lt=Urabe clan|ja|吉田家|1=Urabe clan|2=ja|3=卜部氏|lt=Yoshida family|comment=Might be more of a redirect with potential but this is strictly potential right now|en|draft:Yoshida family|simple|User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|fr|Clan Urabe|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Yoshida family|qq=}}) descend from figures ([[Ame-no-Uzume|Ame no Uzume]], [[Futodama]], {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}}, and {{ill|Ame-no-Koyane|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame no Koyane|qq=}} respectively) played roles in the myth of Amaterasu in the cave.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|59}}

The {{ill|Mononobe clan|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Mononobe clan|qq=}} considered themselves excluded from this, and their ancestor {{ill|Nigihayahi|fr|4=simple|5=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Nigihayahi|qq=}} was excluded. For this reason they wrote the {{ill|Kujiki|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kujiki|qq=}}.  They were highly influential in the development of the department of divinities, but they were not a priestly clan. The Inbe felt their role was minimized so they wrote the {{ill|Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shūi|lt=Kogo Shui|en|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Kogo Shui|qq=}} to improve their position too.<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />

== History ==
[[File:Nihongi_by_Aston_djvu_109.jpg|left|thumb|Sarutahiko and Ame no Uzume, the founders of the clan]]The tales tell of great rivalry between Amaterasu and Susano'o. When he was to leave {{ill|Heaven|en|Heaven|WD=Q4489450|lt=Heaven|1=Heaven}} forever because Izanagi ordered him to, he went to say goodbye to his sister. Amaterasu, suspicious, proposed him a challenge: each of them was to turn an object of the other's into people. Amaterasu created three women from Susanoo's sword while he created five men from her {{ill|Necklace|en|Necklace|WD=Q189299|lt=Necklace|1=Necklace}}. Amaterasu said the men were hers because they were born of her necklace. Susano'o destroyed her {{ill|Rice|en|Rice|WD=Q5090|lt=Rice|1=Rice}} fields, threw a dead {{ill|Pony|en|Pony|WD=Q188828|lt=Pony|1=Pony}} into her {{ill|Loom|en|Loom|WD=Q173056|lt=Loom|1=Loom}}, and killed one of her assistants in {{ill|Anger|en|Anger|WD=Q79871|lt=Anger|1=Anger}}. For this, Amaterasu, sad, angry and scared, went to hide inside [[:en:Ama-no-Iwato|Ama-no-Iwato]], the ''"heavenly rock {{ill|Cave|en|Cave|WD=Q35509|lt=Cave|1=Cave}}"'', so the Sun was hidden and the world became dark for a long time. The [[:en:Oni (folklore)|Oni]] ({{ill|Devil|en|Devil|WD=Q6674|lt=devils|1=Devil}} of Japanese mythology) came out to the dark world, and the gods could not make Amaterasu come out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

The intelligent goddess of {{ill|Happiness|en|Happiness|WD=Q8|lt=Happiness|1=Happiness}}, [[Ame-no-Uzume]] (天宇受売命), took a big bucket, turned it upside down near the cave entrance, and began a dance on it, tearing off her clothing in front of the other Kami. They thought this was so funny that they laughed happily..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

Amaterasu heard them, and looked out to see why the gods were laughing. When she opened the cave, she saw her wonderful reflection in a {{ill|Mirror|en|Mirror|WD=Q35197|lt=Mirror|1=Mirror}} Uzume had put on a tree, and slowly came out of the cave..<ref name="hardacre-2017a" />{{rp|53-68}}

In Ancient times Amaterasu ordered Uzume to accompany her grandson {{ill|Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi-no-Mikoto|lt=Ninigi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ninigi|qq=}} on his journey to earth. They headed to ''{{ill|Ame-no-ukihashi|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-ukihashi|qq=}}'' ("floating bridge of heaven") so they could head to earth but they were blocked by {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}. Uzume came and persuaded Sarutahiko to let Ninigi pass, in other versions of the story Uzume flirts with Sarutahiko.

Later, {{ill|Ame-no-Uzume|lt=Uzume|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ame-no-Uzume|qq=}} and Sarutahiko fall in love and get married. Together, they found the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="picken-2004a">{{Cite book |last=Picken |first=Stuart D. B. |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=BKAhUVqKFhgC&q=Uzume&pg=PA1 |title=Sourcebook in Shinto: Selected Documents |date=2004 |publisher=Greenwood Publishing Group |isbn=978-0-313-26432-0 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="roberts-2009a">{{Cite book |last=Roberts |first=Jeremy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=xdfgjV2kw6oC&q=Uzume |title=Japanese Mythology A to Z |date=2009 |publisher=Infobase Publishing |isbn=978-1-4381-2802-3 |language=en}}</ref><ref name="coulter-2013a">{{Cite book |last1=Coulter |first1=Charles Russell |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=VWxekbhM1yEC&dq=Ame-no-Uzume&pg=PT91 |title=Encyclopedia of Ancient Deities |last2=Turner |first2=Patricia |date=2013-07-04 |publisher=Routledge |isbn=978-1-135-96397-2 |language=en}}</ref>

The Kogo Shui says that this is the origin of a rite done by the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

The Kojiki says that during her time in Ise, Uzume ensured the fish pledged their allegiance to Ninigi. The {{ill|sea cucumber|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/sea cucumber|qq=}}, lacking a mouth, was unable to speak, so Uzume cut a mouth for it. This narrative depicts the Sarume no kimi as the initial recipients of offerings at Ise.<ref name="國學院大學デジタルミュージアム" />

Later in their history they are said to have interbred with the {{ill|Wani clan|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani clan|qq=}}<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref> Which is believed to be related to {{ill|Wani (dragon)|lt=Wani dragons|en|simple|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Wani (dragon)|qq=}}, with Naniwa-neko Takefurukuma described as an ancestor. Marrying women of the Wani clan was believed to give the Emperor control over the sea.<ref name="Akima-1993a">{{Cite journal|last=Akima|first=Toshio|date=1993|title=The Origins of the Grand Shrine of Ise and the Cult of the Sun Goddess Amaterasu Ōmikami|url=https://www.jstor.org/stable/25790929|journal=Japan Review|issue=4|pages=141–198|issn=0915-0986}}</ref>{{Rp|page=149-150}} The wani clan had a similar religious role to the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} as mediums, so many women of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}} had husbands of the Wani clan perform ritual roles as substitutes for men of the {{ill|Sarume clan|lt=Sarume clan|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|en:draft|6=ja|7=猿女君|8=fr|9=Clan Sarume|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarume clan|qq=}}.<ref name="Akima-1993a" />{{Rp|page=168}} Their female dancers did many dances that eventually seemed to fuse with the ceremonies of the Miko. Later on records of the Sarume disappeared.<ref name="Ortolani-1995" />

[[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] in Ise is linked to the same founding myth. The priests of the shrine are said to also be descendants of {{ill|Sarutahiko Ōkami|en|simple|User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|6=fr|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Sarutahiko Ōkami|qq=}}.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Dedicated to Sarutahiko Okami, the Kami of Guidance｜みちひらきの大神 猿田彦神社|url=https://www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp/english/|access-date=2023-10-21|website=www.sarutahikojinja.or.jp}}</ref> who it worships.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2022-01-22|title=Sarutahiko {{!}} 國學院大學デジタルミュージアム|url=https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220122143817/https://d-museum.kokugakuin.ac.jp/eos/detail/?id=9158|archive-date=2022-01-22|access-date=2023-12-07}}</ref>

There is a Sarume shrine which is a subshrine of [[Sarutahiko Shrine|Sarutahiko Shrine]] dedicated to them.<ref name="web.archive.org-2023a" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2022" /><ref name="web.archive.org-2023b" /><ref name="www.kankomie.or.jp" />
